decision.observation: 5 mph, gear 1, first dot filled. The car has turned to face up-frame on grass; a boulder sits just off its right flank, another further left, and the gravel road crosses diagonally ahead and to the right, running from upper-left down past a white rail fence to the bottom-right.
decision.hypothesis: The nose is now aligned with open grass running up toward the road crossing at the top of the frame, so a plain throttle beat should carry the car onto the gravel without needing a costly steer beside the boulder.
decision.memory: W+A from the boulder pin rotated the car without a stall (0 to 5 mph) and aimed it at the road crossing. Forward beats that avoid nearby rocks beat steering beats when the nose already points roughly at the road.
